Hi Sofia / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap / next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard (summary):
- Workload: clinical-assistant workflows + document ingestion for patient records (~2M tokens/day initially, could grow).
- SLOs: 99th percentile latency target ~200ms for single-turn responses; bursty peak traffic during business hours.
- Security: PHI in some flows; customer data residency (US-only) required.
- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, but evaluating Private VPC/on-prem for PHI-sensitive workloads. Hosted API still on the table for non-PHI/lightweight features.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I'll share a cost comparison (hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) with example commits and break-even points — see attached spreadsheet (Redwood_Capacity_vs_API_Pricing.xlsx).
2) Can you confirm the expected sustained qps / tokens per minute during peak hours (ballpark is fine)? This will help size a Dedicated pool vs hosted spend.
3) Sofia — you mentioned a PoC timeline. Are you targeting a March start for a 4-week PoC? If yes, we'll prioritize the capacity plan + security checklist.

Notes about tradeoffs (high-level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, usage-based billing (per-token). Good for lower volume and rapid testing; limited to our hosted regions (we support US-only).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly commits) with much lower per-token compute costs at scale and stronger data isolation. Requires a 1-3 week provisioning lead time for reserved pools depending on size.
- Private VPC / On-prem: highest control for data residency & network isolation; larger upfront investment (license + infra) and longer lead time. Best if you must keep PHI on customer-managed network.

I've cc'd Marissa and Neha so we can loop in pricing + security as needed. Attached is the initial spreadsheet; I'll follow up with a short proposal and SOW draft.

Regards,

Sofia — thanks, answers below and attached is the spreadsheet with line-item math. I pulled conservative numbers for sizing (2M tokens/day sustained) — happy to re-run if you give peak qps.

Ballpark economics (for 2M tokens/day baseline):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~ $3,000 per 1M tokens (equivalent: ~$6,000/day for 2M tokens) — easiest to start, no infra commitment.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): example 4x A100-equivalent pool with a monthly reserved commit of $45,000/month. At 2M tokens/day, that works out to ~ $1,125 per 1M tokens effective (rough calc including average utilization). With higher utilization the effective rate improves.
- Private VPC / On-prem: typical pattern is a one-time platform + license fee (~$250k) + hardware (customer-procured or via partner) and ongoing ops (~$15k/month). For sizing similar throughput, amortized over 24 months this yields ~ $1,500–$2,000 per 1M tokens depending on HW amortization and ops staffing.

Key tradeoffs:
- If you expect steady high volume (>= 1.5–2M tokens/day sustained), Dedicated becomes cost-effective within 2–3 months vs Hosted.
- Private is primarily for regulatory/data-control reasons; unit economics are similar or slightly worse than Dedicated once you include ops and infra amortization.

Security answers:
- SOC2: we can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA / connector for procurement.
- KMS/HSM: Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integration for on-prem.

Attachments: Redwood_Capacity_vs_API_Pricing.xlsx (line-item cost model)

Next steps:
- If you confirm PoC start (target week of Mar 2), we will: 1) provision temporary Dedicated capacity for the PoC, 2) provide security docs + SOC2 excerpt, 3) prepare SOW draft for a 12-week evaluation.
- I'll also schedule a capacity-sizing call — link: https://calendly.com/aditya-rao/redwood-cost-modeling

Happy to hop on a quick call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Aditya

Marissa / Neha — internal note (do not share externally yet).

Summary: Acme Health is evaluating Dedicated vs Private for PHI. They have ~2M tokens/day baseline and want a March PoC. Procurement will ask for a simple TCO comparison and a PoC-friendly commitment.

Proposed pricing posture:
- PoC (4 weeks): provide temporary Dedicated pool at no charge (we cover incremental infra) in exchange for a short PoC MOU and data controls checklist signed.
- Commercial: propose a 12-month reserved commit. Recommend starting commit at $40k/month for 4x A100-equivalent pool (we can offer 10% discount for an annual contract) — effective ~$1,000–$1,200 per 1M tokens at their projected utilization.
- Hosted addendum: keep hosted rates as listed; offer a blended enterprise rate for burst traffic if they want hybrid model.

Approvals / asks:
1) Marissa — can you draft a SOW + pricing term for 12-month commit and attach our standard security annex? Target to send to Sofia by Mon EOD.
2) Neha — confirm if SOC2 excerpt + KMS integration note is ready to send under existing NDA; if we need an additional redaction, flag it.

Notes: procurement may push for a lower/monthly commit. We should be willing to flex to $35k/month with a 12-month locked commitment and 6% uplift to account for expected lower utilization.

- Aditya
